title: Possibilistic Epistemic Game Theory: Earning the Right to Act Among Agents with Different Histories
content: The decisions that most affect people and the planet are made between agents with different histories, where one confident mistake can’t be undone: operators deciding who maneuvers in a crowded orbit, inspectors and the assets they approach, delegations testing whether restraint means anything, incident commanders deciding whose account of a fire line to trust, communities deciding what inherited knowledge to keep. In these settings no probability law for the other side’s behavior is defensible, and what matters is what an agent has earned the right to conclude and to do. Possibilistic Epistemic Game Theory (PEGT) is a game theory for that question. Players hold possibility fields over the world and over each other to a finite depth, updated by the minimum conjunction of the Theory of Epistemic Abductive Geometry (TEAG); every hypothesis carries an epistemic age, the evidence it has survived; there is no common prior and no rationality axiom; and players share only physical spacetime, which decides what evidence reaches each of them and when. We prove that under the requirement that an irreversible action be safe at every hypothesis the evidence still admits, acting on the earned support is the unique maximal safe rule: any method that acts more has an environment, consistent with all its evidence, in which it causes harm. We give the experiments that earn warrant at least harm within a budget, and show that a contained trial of an action can earn the right to take it while no evidence can earn warrant against behavior an agent hasn’t modeled. We characterize the smallest part of a player’s state that predicts its behavior, give a necessary and sufficient condition for epistemic age to lower worst-case loss, show that an agent’s own field, kept apart from what it was told, carries exactly the warrant the full record does, and bound what any observer can learn about intent from the stakes it has tested. Players coordinate safely without agreeing, hold an epistemic fixed point under admitted actions, and deform one another only through retarded physical evidence, so that every disagreement between them has an address in spacetime. In nineteen pre-registered studies on more than half a million human decisions and on constructed problems, PEGT observers kept 2,492 of 2,881 betrayals admissible where a Bayesian credible set kept 341, judged their own reliability to within 0.012 without knowing the truth, flagged every game against a partner their library couldn’t represent, and showed that people hold inherited expectations as texture that decisive experience overrides. Under the warrant requirement, the earned-support rule violated warrant in none of 400 random worlds while merged declarations violated it in all and credible sets in some at every level, and with graduated authorization it completed 125,941 safe irreversible actions. A comparative analysis against Bayesian methods shows where each standard applies: under the warrant requirement PEGT’s rule is the one that never harms, and where the score rewards betting on frequencies a Bayesian bets better, for reasons the analysis makes exact.
